title: Palantir Stock Is Near Its Record. Here's the Price at Which I'd Buy It.
detail:
Palantir Stock Is Near Its Record. Here's the Price at Which I'd Buy It.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 7:57 AM MST 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) ended Oct. 9 at $209.05, their highest close ever. They've dipped since. But at around $198 as I write, the stock still sits only about 5% under that high.

It's easy to see why investors keep paying up. The artificial intelligence (AI) data and analytics specialist grew its second-quarter revenue 93% year over year, and its profits rose even faster.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But at today's price, investors pay around 170 times earnings for it, going by what Palantir earned in the last year -- more than I'm willing to pay.

At what price, then, would the stock become a buy for me?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Palantir's profits keep climbing

Highlighting how fast the company is scaling, Palantir's second-quarter earnings per share more than tripled year over year, up from $0.13 to $0.41. Net income grew a bit faster still, hitting around $1.06 billion versus about $327 million in the year-ago quarter. Earlier quarters showed the same climb. Palantir's quarterly earnings per share rose from $0.18 in the third quarter of 2025 to $0.24 in the fourth quarter, then to $0.34 in the first quarter of 2026 before hitting $0.41 in the second.

Add those four quarters up, and Palantir earned $1.17 per share over the last year. That's almost four times the $0.30 per share it earned in the four quarters before.

I'll use that trailing $1.17 as my earnings figure, because it's what the company reported, not an estimate.

Of course, the quarter-to-quarter gains are shrinking. Earnings per share rose around 42% from the fourth quarter to the first quarter, but only about 21% from the first quarter to the second.

Even for a business growing so fast, paying about 170 times earnings of $1.17 a share is a lot for profits that have already been booked.

What did investors pay at the low?

To choose a valuation multiple, I don't have to guess what a fast-growing software business might deserve. Palantir showed what investors were willing to pay for it just a few months ago.

On June 25, shares ended at around $107, the lowest closing price over the last 12 months. At that time, Palantir's trailing earnings per share came to $0.89, based on the four quarters through March. So, even near the bottom of a tough first half, investors paid around 120 times earnings.

title: Does The Move In Snowflake Stock Change Anything?

Does The Move In Snowflake Stock Change Anything?

Image from Pexels

Snowflake (SNOW) stock rose 59.3% from January 18 to October 15, 2026, against 12.5% for the S&P 500. The company reported quarterly results three times along the way, on February 25, May 27 and September 2. Buyers appear to be betting that customers using AI on Snowflake's data platform will keep its sales growth climbing while its losses shrink. So how much faster is Snowflake growing than it was in January?

Snowflake Has Grown Faster Every Quarter Since January

Snowflake's revenue is growing about five percentage points faster than when the rise began. Revenue grew 30.1% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026, the quarter that ended January 31. That pace reached 35.1% in fiscal Q2 2027, with growth registering higher in each quarter along the way. Product revenue, nearly all of Snowflake's sales, grew 37% in that latest quarter. On the September 2 call, management said customers using AI on Snowflake consume more across the data platform.

The stock's two largest one-day gains during the rise came right after the May 27 and September 2 reports. Shares rose 37% on May 28, the day after Snowflake reported fiscal Q1 2027 results. On the September 2 call, management said it had raised its fiscal 2027 forecast for product revenue growth by more than five percentage points, to 36%. The stock gained 16.6% the next day.

A run higher can leave Snowflake a larger share of what you own than you planned. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Far Have Snowflake's Losses Shrunk?

Snowflake's operating loss came to 17.0% of revenue in fiscal Q2 2027, against 29.7% in fiscal Q2 2026. The company's losses are narrowing, though it still loses money. Management said on the September 2 call that Snowflake remains on track for a profit under standard accounting rules (GAAP) in fiscal Q4 2028.

Yet management also said its fast-growing AI workloads carry a lower margin today. So Snowflake keeps less of each dollar on the sales that are lifting its growth, at least for now.

Why Snowflake Is Still Valued On Its Sales

Snowflake is still valued on its sales because it remains unprofitable, despite the faster growth. It lost $1.09 billion over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, so its price-to-earnings multiple is not meaningful. Its operating loss over those twelve months stood at 22.8% of revenue. That marks the smallest figure at any quarter end from fiscal Q2 2021 on, yet it is still a loss.

On sales, the stock trades at 21.5 times, against 3.1 for the S&P 500. At that multiple, the share price appears to assume that both the faster growth and the shrinking losses continue.

Welcome to Episode #503 of the Zacks Market Edge Podcast.

Every week, host and Zacks stock strategist, Tracey Ryniec, is joined by guests to discuss the hottest investing topics in stocks, bonds, and ETFs and how it impacts your life.

This week, Tracey went solo to talk about stocks that are breaking out, instead of breaking down. October has been rough for some stocks, including many of the AI Revolution stocks.

Why not talk about stocks that are doing well instead?

Tracey did not run a screen to find these stocks. She has been tracking some of them herself. She also owns AbbVie in the Zacks Value Investor and in her own personal portfolio.

These are stock ideas for those who think everything is gloomy right now.

There's always a bull market somewhere.

5 Stock Ideas for Your Short List

1. Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR)

Palantir is a software company which bills itself as the "foundational software of tomorrow." In the second quarter, Palantir grew revenue by 93% year-over-year. It also raised FY2026 revenue guidance.

Shares of Palantir are trading near all-time highs but are up just 12.8% year-to-date. Palantir is expected to grow earnings in FY 2026 by 118.7% and another 40.9% in FY 2027.

Palantir is not cheap. It trades with a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of 122.

For investors looking for a growth company, Palantir should be on your short list.

2. BP p.l.c. (BP)

BP is a global energy company with oil and natural gas production and refining. It is what many refer to as "big oil."

Shares of bp are up 39.5% year-to-date and are at new 5-year highs. Earnings are expected to jump 162.8% in 2026 thanks to high oil prices due to the Iran War.

BP is cheap. It trades with a P/E of 6.5. A P/E under 10 usually indicates a company is a deep value.

BP is also shareholder friendly. In the second quarter of 2026, bp raised the dividend 4%. It is currently yielding an attractive 4.2%.

BP is also a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). It will report third quarter earnings on Oct 30, 2026.

For investors looking for a way to play the high oil prices, bp should be on your short list.

3. Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (PANW)

Palo Alto Networks is a global cybersecurity company with a market cap of $300 billion.

Shares of Palo Alto Networks are near their all-time highs and are up 101% year-to-date. It's a growth stock. Earnings are expected to rise 8.8% in fiscal 2027 and another 17.5% in fiscal 2028.

ARK also sold 31,432 shares of Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) that day, worth about $6.3 million. The dollar value of the Thursday buy was not reported.

CoreWeave's market value is $38.44 billion, so these purchases show conviction but are far too small to hold up the price.

Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Over the past month, shares of this company have returned +13.8%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Palantir Technologies falls in, has gained 5.4%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Palantir Technologies is expected to post earnings of $0.42 per share, indicating a change of +100% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.64 points to a change of +118.7% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +2.4%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $2.31 indicates a change of +41.1% from what Palantir Technologies is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Palantir Technologies.

What Happened?

Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) and Apple each committed $25 million to President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday.

The report showed total private donations of $333 million for the project.

Others gave $25 million too, including the Adelson family and Dish Network co-founder Charles Ergen. Lockheed Martin, Microsoft and Palantir each gave $10 million. The president is not on the donor list, per the Post.

Nvidia said it was proud to support a nonpartisan trust, and a spokesperson said its support for the U.S. is independent of any business interests.

Apple declined to comment.

The White House said it will not release donor details.

NVDA Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

The project has drawn criticism.

Watchdog groups say the secrecy raises questions about donor influence. The Post said half the money came from companies or executives with federal contracts.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Nvidia Stock

$25 million is tiny compared with Nvidia's size, so the donation alone is unlikely to move Nvidia stock much.

The business is what drives Nvidia stock.

In Q2, revenue hit $96 billion, more than double last year.

Data center sales rose 18% from the prior quarter to $89 billion.

Management guided Q3 revenue to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

It expects about 70% revenue growth next fiscal year, limited by supply.

Nvidia also returned a record $26 billion to shareholders in Q2.

Nvidia stock faces risks beyond this headline as memory costs are rising fast.

Management expects gross margin to fall to 71%-72% in Q4 and also said it has no China data center revenue in its outlook.

And some critics call its investments in AI labs "circular financing," which Nvidia disputes.

Still, the market tends to focus on demand.

The CEO said demand far outpaces supply. For now, Nvidia stock rests on AI spending, not on the ballroom story.

The reputational risk is worth watching if scrutiny grows.

title: Defense ETFs in Spotlight Ahead of Q3 Earnings Season

The U.S. defense sector faces an unusually turbulent third-quarter earnings season, a development rarely seen over the past decade. Caused by uncertainty over U.S. military spending ahead of November midterms, slowing airline traffic growth, and lingering supply-chain constraints, the S&P 1500 Aerospace and Defense Index fell nearly 19% from its early-August high through Oct. 15, 2026. 

As the sector gears up for the third-quarter 2026 earnings next week, investors must be shifting focus from geopolitical headlines to hard balance sheets, particularly for stocks like Lockheed Martin LMT and RTX Corp. RTX, both scheduled to post results early next week.

This reporting cycle should serve as a critical stress test, revealing whether record-breaking backlogs from prior spending pledges are converting into meaningful bottom-line growth amid a skeptical market environment.

Factors Likely to Have Shaped Defense Stocks in Q3

Heading into third-quarter earnings, prominent defense stocks are caught between two opposing forces: robust spending commitments and a punishing interest-rate environment that has fundamentally altered how the market values growth.

The single most important factor has been the recent surge in U.S. Treasury yields, with the 10-year rate breaking above 5% for the first time since 2007. This has hit defense stocks harder than most sectors because their earnings are heavily weighted toward future backlogs. 

This is because, despite delivering healthy revenue growth and backlogs, these defense stocks are now being valued at a higher cost of capital, thanks to sticky inflation and a higher interest rate environment.

Meanwhile, the geopolitical backdrop has been a double-edged sword. Escalation risks in Ukraine and the Middle East are real, but geopolitical headlines alone are no longer expected to boost defense stocks' quarterly results. As the market has shifted from pricing the probability of conflict to pricing the execution of contracts and the cost of capital, close scrutiny will remain on the cash flow generation capacity of the prominent defense stocks this time. 

Despite these valuation headwinds, several underlying factors are expected to have supported the sector's quarterly performance. Sustained NATO spending commitments, a steady flow of awarded contracts, and resilient demand for defense electronics and munitions should have translated into solid top-line growth. Diversified players with exposure to cybersecurity and sensor systems have likely benefited from AI-driven demand. These drivers, combined with cost discipline and favorable program mix, are expected to have offset some of the margin pressure from higher interest rates.
